hook.text: Arabic letters change shape depending on where they appear in a word—initial, medial, final, or isolated.

buildup.text: Arabic script is cursive by design—letters connect to each other within words.

discovery.text: Written right to left, Arabic script has been adapted for Persian, Urdu, Pashto, and many more.

twist.text: Arabic calligraphy became an art form because Islam discouraged figurative images in sacred spaces.

climax.text: Arabic is the second most widely used script in the world after Latin.

punchline.text: Letters flow into each other—script as art.

quiz.question: Why do Arabic letters change shape?
options: Their form depends on position within the word
Each writer has a different style
